claims.text: The target material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature produce accelerated coupled degradation.
Micro-galvanic coupling between different phases is the primary cause of the accelerated coupled degradation.
Micro-galvanic coupling between phases causes selective dissolution of one or more phases.
The degradation mechanism includes formation of a protective oxide layer.
A protective oxide layer can improve elevated-temperature wear resistance.
The multi-phase alloy will have an increased wear rate under the coupled exposure relative to the baseline.
The multi-phase alloy will have an increased corrosion rate under the coupled exposure relative to the baseline.
The multi-phase alloy will have greater total degradation than a single-phase alloy or an alloy without micro-galvanic coupling.
The proposed mechanism applies at elevated temperature in a corrosive environment.
A single-phase alloy or an alloy without micro-galvanic coupling is an appropriate baseline.
A controlled comparison using wear rate, corrosion rate, and microstructural analysis can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the multi-phase alloy to show accelerated coupled degradation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes a protective oxide layer while predicting increased wear and corrosion rates. The hypothesis does not explain why the protective effect is insufficient, disrupted by wear, or otherwise contributes to acceleration; the cited wear evidence instead associates oxide formation with increased wear resistance.
